title: ShapeShifter (WIP title)
author: angrylittledev
selftext:
I came up with the idea of making a game that's set in the time of the Vikings, you're a drifter human that discovers powers of transformation, you explore the story, find runes, unlock new forms, help the villagers until you become one of them. The game allows you to transform freely from Human to wolf, to raven, to fish, to mole, to bear and owl. Will add more water forms in the future. 

What you see here is just models loaded into the three.js, made with Claude 4.7 Opus, my own art and models in Trellis and Trellis too. Models aren't rigged yet, so that's gonna be next, but wanted to replace all the basic models in game with my own GLB's. Game has a night and day cycle. Human and animal enemies, mole can dig under the ground for relics and what not, if you try fish on land you will die :D

comments.author: LaetoStudio
comments.body:
The shapeshifting concept sounds fun and I feel like it's underutilized in games today. Transforming as a druid in WoW back in the day will always be a fond memory for me.  
I'm curious to see where you take the game!

replies.author: angrylittledev
replies.body: Yeah I agree, shapeshifting needs to come back.. But this is a simple browser game, I just hope to rig the models properly and tell a decent story, the graphics won't be that great unfortunately.

comments.author: Felfedezni
comments.body: Looks like mm6 which is good and bad.

replies.author: angrylittledev
replies.body: Oh I see, well not really, the graphics are about 30y ahead, but like I said this is just models loaded in, nothing is rigged, I still have to add textures to water, ground, grass, etc. I'll work on making it look better, plus I went more for anime art style for characters and animals. It's a long road ahead, I'm still fixing the underground mechanic and environment for mole transformation.

replies.author: Felfedezni
replies.body: Just the first impression I got.

replies.author: darktaco
replies.body:
"Went more for anime art style for characters and animals" and "graphics are about 30y ahead" is in reference to...the video you posted? I mean, I suppose, technically, the graphics are indeed 30 years ahead, but...I'm not sure the video posted is 30 years ahead from an art direction standpoint, or at least it's unclear from the video. Not trying to hate, I think a shapeshifting game would be cool.

But there is more than a bit of texturing and rigging that is going to make a shapeshifting game memorable.

replies.author: angrylittledev
replies.body: Omg I already said, these are just static GLB's loaded into Three,js with no effects, no rigging, everything is just bare bones just to show the concept of the game. Why are you acting like this is the final product?

comments.author: lordpoee
comments.body:
Two things,  
Learn about rigging, how to animate your models  
if this is called shifter you'll want to build animated morph effects, players will see this a lot so make it interesting, maybe even make the shifting interactive ie pressing a combination of arrows to take that form, more powerful forms could have more complicated patterns. Just some ideas.
